faqs.answer: Because both pans hold the same volume: 8 cups each. The loaf pan is narrower but deeper, and the round pan is wider but shallower, and the two differences cancel out exactly.
faqs.question: Why doesn't the batter change?

faqs.answer: Area only measures the floor, and it ignores depth. A 9x5 loaf covers 45 square inches and a 9-inch round covers 63.6, but the loaf pan is 2.75 inches deep against the round pan 2 inches. For pans of different depths, volume is the honest comparison.
faqs.question: Why does area maths give a different answer?

faqs.answer: Yes for quick breads, banana bread, zucchini bread, and butter cakes. They bake like a snack cake in a round pan and slice into wedges. Yeast breads do not suit the swap, because a loaf shape is part of how they bake.
faqs.question: Will a loaf recipe work as a round cake?

faqs.answer: Start checking 10 to 15 minutes before the loaf bake time, following King Arthur guidance for a shallower pan. A 60-minute loaf is usually done between 45 and 55 minutes in a round pan, but trust the toothpick, not the clock.
faqs.question: How much faster does it bake?

faqs.answer: An 8-inch round holds 6 cups, so scale the batter by 0.75 and bake the extra separately. The smaller pan also bakes deeper, so expect the full loaf time or a few minutes longer.
faqs.question: Can I use an 8-inch round instead?

felicityNote: Banana bread in a round pan is still banana bread. It just slices into wedges, which makes it feel like cake, and nobody complains.

title: Loaf Pan to 9-Inch Round Converter
tutorial: This swap is a time swap, not a batter swap. A 9x5 loaf pan holds 8 cups and a 9-inch round pan holds 8 cups, so the volume factor is 8 divided by 8, which is 1. The batter goes in unchanged. What changes is how deep it sits, and depth is what decides the bake time.

Area maths would mislead you here, and it is worth knowing why. A 9x5 loaf covers 45 square inches of floor and a 9-inch round covers 63.6, so the area ratio says 1.41. But the loaf pan is 2.75 inches deep and the round is 2 inches deep, and the extra depth is where the loaf pan holds its volume. Compare pans of different depths by volume, not by floor, or the answer comes out wrong.

A loaf recipe baked in a round pan becomes a snack cake. Banana bread, zucchini bread, and pound cake all bake well flat, and they slice into wedges instead of slabs, which suits a coffee cake served at the table. The crumb stays the same. Only the shape changes, and the shape is serving, not baking.

The bake is shorter, because the batter sits shallower. A loaf that takes 60 minutes in a 9x5 pan can be done 10 to 15 minutes sooner in a round pan, following King Arthur guidance for a larger, shallower pan. Start checking at 45 minutes for a 60-minute loaf, and use a toothpick in the center. A round cake hides a wet middle well, and the top browns before the center sets.

Keep the fill under two-thirds, which is about 5.3 cups in a 9-inch round. A loaf recipe that makes 5 cups of batter fits fine. A recipe that makes 6 cups is over the line in the round pan, even though it fit the loaf pan, because the loaf pan is deeper. Bake the extra cup in a ramekin rather than overfilling the round.
